audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor may be mislabeled and stale relative to the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: The $340.5 million anchor ends January 31, 2026, while the bridge is dated August 1, 2026; subsequent 26-week net income was $344.451 million and included a $169.5 million pretax tariff-refund benefit, of which $163.6 million entered cost of goods sold and $5.9 million entered interest and other income. The resulting valuation adjustment is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: A current trailing owner-earnings calculation could change the anchor and every scenario's operating present value; using August cash and September shares against January earnings also creates an inconsistent valuation date.
audit_findings.evidence: References to "fiscal year 2025" or "fiscal 2025" refer to the period from February 2, 2025 to January 31, 2026, which consists of a 52-week fiscal year.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrably calls the completed January 2026 period fiscal 2025, although a calendar year-ending convention could explain the series label. The economically important issue is demonstrated: the anchor omits six months of filed results while the bridge uses August balances. Those results changed substantially, but the large tariff refund must be removed and interim capital needs normalized, so the direction cannot be inferred safely. The change is reasonably capable of materially altering the modeled values even though the current $252.20 price remains far above the reported $121.73 bull value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild trailing owner earnings through August 1, 2026 by adding fiscal-2026 first-half OE and removing the comparable fiscal-2025 first half from the January annual figure; purge the $169.5 million pretax tariff-refund benefit and portfolio interest, normalize capital spending, then rerun the anchor and all scenarios using the August bridge and September share count.

audit_findings.title: The bridge assumes all cash and short-term investments are excess
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $1,187.904 million, equal to $21.16 per share and 19.9% of the $5.972 billion base equity value; the actual operating-cash reserve is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for inventory, payroll, rent, distribution and seasonal liquidity must be excluded from the excess-cash bridge rather than added to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary working capital requirements are for the purchase of store inventory and payment of payroll, rent, other store operating costs and distribution costs.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the full balance is demonstrated, but the record does not demonstrate how much is distributable or prove that a particular reserve was omitted. The exposure is material because the added balance supplies nearly one-fifth of base equity value. Removing required operating cash would reduce intrinsic value and the buy-below price, although it would reinforce rather than reverse the present overvaluation versus the market price.
audit_findings.action: Use monthly or weekly cash, investment, inventory, payable and revolver data across the seasonal peak to establish minimum operating liquidity; exclude card-settlement receivables and other operating balances as appropriate, add only distributable surplus, and rerun the bridge, per-share values and buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: The owner-earnings anchor may understate recurring capital needs
audit_findings.magnitude: The latest fiscal-2026 capital-expenditure plan is $250-$260 million, $75.259-$85.259 million above fiscal-2025 actual capital expenditures of $174.741 million, equal to 22.1%-25.0% of the $340.5 million anchor; the recurring-maintenance portion is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Understated maintenance capital expenditure inflates normalized owner earnings and all operating present values; growth capital already represented by the RONTA reinvestment charge must not be deducted twice.
audit_findings.evidence: We plan to make cash capital expenditures of approximately $230 million to $250 million in fiscal 2026, which exclude the impact of tenant allowances, and which we expect to fund from cash generated from operations, cash on-hand, investments and, as needed, borrowings under our Revolving Credit Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: No anchor error is yet demonstrated. The plan is forward-looking and includes approximately $100 million for new stores, while the remainder combines remodels, relocations, corporate infrastructure and shipcenter work whose maintenance-versus-growth classification is unavailable. The total increase is large enough to matter if recurring, but the supplied record cannot establish the sustainable deduction or its materiality after avoiding double-counted growth reinvestment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile fiscal-2025 and trailing fiscal-2026 capital expenditures by project, tenant allowance and asset class; classify new stores, capacity expansion and genuinely recurring maintenance separately, compare recurring spending with depreciation and the anchor deduction, and rerun OE only for any demonstrated maintenance shortfall.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved securities and derivative litigation could create a senior cash claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A settlement, judgment, deductible or uninsured defense cost would reduce excess cash or future owner earnings before value reaches common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The potential impact of these actions, which seek unspecified damages, attorneys’ fees and expenses, is uncertain.
audit_findings.explanation: The litigation and its progression are demonstrated, including class certification on August 3, 2026 and additional derivative proceedings, but liability is not demonstrated. The company reports unspecified damages and uncertain impact, and the record supplies neither a loss estimate nor insurance recovery. Management's belief that ultimate resolution will not be material does not quantify the exposure, so materiality remains unresolved rather than established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-filing docket developments, claimed-loss methodology, class size, insurance limits and exclusions, deductibles, defense-cost treatment and any subsequent accrual; deduct a probable estimable net claim from the bridge or normalize recurring legal expense in OE, then rerun if quantified.

audit_findings.title: Deferred compensation is an omitted non-debt claim
audit_findings.magnitude: The actual net obligation is unquantified but is bounded by the latest $11.318 million total other long-term liabilities, equal to approximately $0.20 per share and 0.19% of the $5.972 billion base equity value, before considering matching trust assets.
audit_findings.mechanism: Only an unfunded deferred-compensation obligation whose matching assets are included in the bridge should be deducted as a senior non-debt claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Payments under the Deferred Comp Plan will be made from the general assets of the Company or from the assets of the Trust, funded by the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The plan obligation is demonstrated, but the filing does not disclose its individual amount or show that trust assets are included in cash and short-term investments. Even treating all latest other long-term liabilities as the omitted claim produces only about a 0.19% reduction to base equity value, so it cannot materially change the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Identify the deferred-compensation liability and related trust assets, confirm whether those assets enter the $1.188 billion bridge balance, and deduct only the net unfunded amount for completeness; no material rerun is required unless the liability is found outside the disclosed other-long-term-liabilities total.
